captions.text: a route reads files and calls a costly api, once per distinct body.
f1 has body A. its key is stored, then the api is called.
when the exchange completes, f1 is moved to .camel.
f2 has the same body. the key is already there, so f2 is skipped.
f3 has body B. with eager=true its key is stored before the call.
the jvm crashes before the api is called.
after the restart f3 is still in the inbox, so it is read again.
key B is already in the repository, so f3 counts as a duplicate.
f3 is moved to .camel. the api never got B, and no error is logged.
camel verify does not wait for a crash. it tries one at every step.
it explores every reachable state and keeps the shortest bad run.
the verdict names the guarantee the route really gives.
storing the key after the call (eager=false) swaps loss for a duplicate.
with an api that does not ignore repeats, no setting gives exactly-once.
camel verify tells you which one you have, before you deploy.

title: camel verify
subtitle: a proposal: model-check a camel integration for loss, duplicates and deadlock
